subject: Chemistry
description: Galvanic + electrolytic cells, batteries, electrolysis, electroplating

questions.stem: In a GALVANIC (voltaic) CELL, chemical energy is converted to:
questions.explanation: GALVANIC / VOLTAIC CELL — chemical → electrical energy via SPONTANEOUS redox reaction. Two half-cells with different electrodes (e.g., Zn + Cu); SALT BRIDGE (or porous separator) carries ions; external wire carries electrons. EMF = electrochemical-cell voltage. ELECTROLYTIC CELL — opposite: ELECTRICAL energy drives a NON-SPONTANEOUS reaction (electrolysis). DANIELL CELL (Zn/Cu) = classic galvanic cell; ~1.1 V. PRIMARY cells = single-use (dry cells, alkaline). SECONDARY cells = rechargeable (lead-acid, Li-ion).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: In any electrochemical cell, OXIDATION takes place at:
questions.explanation: Mnemonic: 'AN OX' (Anode = OXidation), 'RED CAT' (REDuction = CAThode). ALWAYS, regardless of cell type. POLARITY differs: in GALVANIC cells, anode is NEGATIVE (gives up electrons); cathode POSITIVE. In ELECTROLYTIC cells, anode is POSITIVE (connected to + terminal of external power source); cathode NEGATIVE. Confuses students! Memory aid: anode = oxidation (always); polarity depends on cell type.

questions.stem: ELECTROPLATING (e.g., gold-plating jewellery, chrome-plating bumpers) uses:

options.option_text: Electrolytic cell driven by external power

questions.explanation: ELECTROPLATING — coats one metal with thin layer of another. Object to be plated = CATHODE; plating metal = ANODE (or in solution as ions). External battery drives the redox: anode dissolves → ions → reduce + deposit on cathode. Examples: silver plating cutlery; gold plating jewellery; chrome plating bumpers; nickel plating tools; tin plating cans. Used to: improve appearance, corrosion-resistance, electrical contact. COMMERCIAL use: huge industry. Distractor 1 — galvanic (spontaneous) doesn't drive plating reliably.

questions.stem: A common LEAD-ACID battery (used in cars) consists of plates of:

options.option_text: Lithium (anode) + cobalt oxide (cathode), in lithium salt

questions.explanation: LEAD-ACID battery (Plante, 1859): Pb anode + PbO₂ cathode, dilute H₂SO₄ (~38%) as electrolyte. Reaction (discharge): Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ → 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O. Each cell ~2.1 V; car battery has 6 cells in series = ~12 V. RECHARGEABLE — reverses reaction during charging. Heavy + bulky but cheap + reliable. Used in: cars (starter battery), UPS, solar storage. Distractor 3 = LECLANCHE (dry) cell = Zn anode + carbon/MnO₂ cathode, NH₄Cl paste (~1.5 V; non-rechargeable). Distractor 4 = LITHIUM-ION battery (modern, high energy density, smartphones, laptops, EVs).

questions.stem: DRY CELL (small AAA, AA cells) is also called:
questions.explanation: DRY CELL (zinc-carbon, Leclanche cell, 1866): Zn anode (outer casing) + carbon rod cathode in MnO₂ paste with NH₄Cl + ZnCl₂ electrolyte (paste, not liquid → 'dry'). EMF ~1.5 V. PRIMARY (single-use). ALKALINE batteries (better) — KOH electrolyte, longer life, same 1.5 V. BUTTON cells — silver oxide (~1.55 V, watches), lithium (3 V, hearing aids, calculators), zinc-air (~1.4 V, hearing aids — uses atmospheric O₂). Mercury cells (1.35 V) — phasing out due to toxicity.

questions.stem: FUEL CELLS are a special type of electrochemical cell that:

options.option_text: Store fuel internally and discharge slowly over time
Generate electricity continuously from supplied fuel + oxidant
Store electrical charge inside chemical bonds for later use
Burn fuel in air to release heat energy + light only

questions.explanation: FUEL CELL — like a battery but FUEL + OXIDANT are continuously SUPPLIED (don't run out unless supply stops). Most common: HYDROGEN-OXYGEN fuel cell. 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O + electricity. Output: ~70% efficiency (vs 30-40% for combustion engines). Clean: only WATER as exhaust. USED IN: spacecraft (Apollo, Space Shuttle), some buses + cars (Toyota Mirai, Hyundai Nexo), backup power. India's Hydrogen Mission (2021). Limitations: needs pure H₂ (currently mostly from natural gas); H₂ storage difficult.

questions.stem: Aluminium is extracted from BAUXITE by which process?
questions.explanation: HALL-HÉROULT process (1886, independently by Charles Hall + Paul Héroult): Al₂O₃ (alumina, refined from bauxite by Bayer process) dissolved in molten CRYOLITE (Na₃AlF₆) at ~950°C; ELECTROLYSED with carbon electrodes. Cathode reaction: Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al (collected as molten Al at bottom). Anode: O²⁻ → O₂; reacts with carbon → CO₂ (anodes consumed, replaced periodically). Why not smelting with C like iron? Al has very high affinity for O₂ — needs much higher temperature than Fe → impractical with reduction. Energy-intensive: ~13-15 kWh per kg Al → 'frozen electricity'. Recycling Al saves ~95% of energy vs new production.
